name: Gwerz Breton (Brittany narrative-lament)
lineage: Breton gwerz long-narrative-lament tradition of Brittany (Lower Brittany, Breton-language region), comprising the canonical Breton-language sung-narrative corpus addressing historical-tragic events, supernatural-encounters, and personal-moral-cautionary tales. Performance configuration: solo unaccompanied female-or-male voice in characteristic free-rhythm extended-melismatic style with narrow-range modal vocabulary and the strict Breton-Celtic-meter four-line stanza form. The nineteenth-century Théodore Hersart de La Villemarqué Barzaz-Breiz collection (1839) consolidated the literary-historical canon. The post-1970 Breton-language-revival under Yann-Fañch Kemener and Nolwenn Korbell sustained institutional transmission. Distinguished from Breton kan ha diskan dance-singing by gwerz's sung-narrative-without-dance functional orientation.
